title: Bible Data from Christian Pure
description:
Nine open datasets behind the free Bible and church tools at christianpure.com, as CSV, JSON and GeoJSON with Frictionless Data descriptions:

  • bible-places: the 1,247 places the Bible names, from Genesis to Revelation, with coordinates, how sure each location is, the verses that name them and their names in 11 languages; built on OpenBible.info's Bible geocoding, with Pleiades and Wikidata links.
  • topical-bible: over 6,500 Bible subjects and their verse references (no Bible text), from the OpenBible.info Topical Bible and Christian Pure's pages.
  • pauls-journeys: Paul's three missionary journeys and his voyage to Rome, 69 stops and 65 legs, with distances by Roman road and by sea.
  • saints: 378 saints with their feast days in the Western and Orthodox calendars, patronages and 1,090 sources.
  • denominations: 22 churches and traditions, and Protestants in general, on 55 questions, each answered from the church's own documents.
  • easter-dates: Western and Orthodox Easter and the movable feasts for every year from 1900 to 2099.
  • bible-natural-events: 25 earthquakes, eclipses, famines and droughts from the Bible and the early church, each set against earthquake catalogues, eclipse calculations, climate records and ancient historians and given one of four grades, with 218 sources.
  • jerusalem-sky: on which day, and which weekday, did Passover fall in a given year? For every year from 1000 BC to AD 135, worked out from NASA JPL's DE441 ephemeris with Skyfield. Each of the 14,038 months gets the evening the new crescent was most likely first seen from the Temple Mount, and the earliest it could have been, by Yallop's 1997 test. 14 and 15 Nisan and their weekdays follow under both, with the month before and after for years that may have had an extra month. The folder also lists every eclipse seen from Jerusalem, Samaria or Nineveh from 1999 BC to AD 500, and the sky on named nights, among them 3 April AD 33, when the moon rose in eclipse. Every row carries the margin from Earth's uneven spin (Delta T). Julian calendar, with Julian Day Numbers.
  • easter-moons: why do Western and Orthodox Easter fall on different days? For every year from AD 325 to 2100, the full moon of the church's Easter tables beside the real full moon over Jerusalem, with Western, Orthodox and astronomical (Aleppo 1997) Easter. The Julian tables' moon, which the Orthodox churches still use, now runs about four days late; in 32 years of this century it picks the next month's moon, so Orthodox Easter falls four or five weeks after Western Easter.

Everything is under CC BY 4.0 except the Easter dates and the two sky tables, which are CC0, and the natural events, which are CC BY-SA 4.0. Each folder has its own README with sources, limits and how to cite it. Source repository: github.com/christianpure/bible-data.
